chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abd al-Malik ibn Aʿyan or Malik ibn Aʿyan, from Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a Christian man who died, leaving a Muslim son of his brother and a Muslim son of his sister, while the Christian had children and a Christian wife. He said:

I hold that his Muslim brother’s son should be given two-thirds of what he left, and his Muslim sister’s son should be given one-third of what he left, if he has no young children. But if he has young children, then the two heirs must spend on the minors from what they inherited from their father until they reach maturity.

It was said to him: How should they spend on the minors? He said: The heir of the two-thirds share pays two-thirds of the maintenance, and the heir of the one-third share pays one-third of the maintenance. Then when they reach maturity, they stop the maintenance for them.

It was said to him: What if his children embrace Islam while they are young? He said: What their father left should be delivered to the Imam until they reach maturity. If they remain upon Islam when they reach maturity, the Imam gives his inheritance to them. But if they do not remain upon Islam when they reach maturity, the Imam gives his inheritance to his Muslim brother’s son and his Muslim sister’s son: he gives two-thirds of what he left to his brother’s son and one-third of what he left to his sister’s son.

key_terms.النَّفَقَةِ: financial maintenance to be spent on the minors
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the Imam as the authority entrusted with holding the estate
key_terms.مِيرَاثَهُ: his inheritance or estate to be distributed
key_terms.نَصْرَانِيٍّ: a Christian man, whose estate is being discussed
key_terms.وُلْدٌ صِغَارٌ: minor children who have not yet reached maturity

ai.seo_question: How is the inheritance of a Christian divided when Muslim relatives survive him and his children are minors?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the inheritance of a Christian deceased when some relatives are Muslim and his wife and children remain Christian. It explains the division of the estate, the obligation to maintain minor children from the inherited wealth, and the Imam’s role in holding the estate if the children enter Islam before maturity. The narration is significant for jurisprudence on inheritance across different religions and guardianship over the property of minors.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5729 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Hisham ibn Salim from Abd Al-Malik ibn Aʿyan or Malik ibn Aʿyan from Abu Jafar (as) who said:

I asked Imam (as) about a Christian man who died, leaving behind a Muslim nephew (son of his brother) and a Muslim niece (daughter of his sister), while his own children and wife were Christians.
Imam (as) said:

"I see that the Muslim nephew should be given two-thirds of what he left behind, and the Muslim niece should be given one-third of what he left behind, provided he does not have young children. However, if he has young children, then the two heirs must provide for the children from what they inherited from their father until the children reach maturity."

It was asked: "How should they provide for the children?"
Imam (as) replied: "The heir of the two-thirds share must cover two-thirds of the expenses, and the heir of the one-third share must cover one-third of the expenses. Once the children mature, the heirs are no longer responsible for their expenses."

It was then asked: "What if his children embrace Islam while they are still young?"
Imam (as) said: "In that case, what their father left behind should be handed over to the Imam until they reach maturity. If they remain steadfast in Islam upon reaching maturity, the Imam will give them their inheritance. But if they do not remain in Islam upon maturity, the Imam will return the inheritance to the Muslim nephew and niece, giving the nephew two-thirds of what was left and the niece one-third."
